---
title: "NBA MVP MACHINE"
format: html
---

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show code"
import pandas as pd
from itables import show
from shared import build_players_df

players_df = build_players_df()
players_df['MVP Rank'] = players_df['mvp_score'].rank(ascending= False, method='min').astype('Int64')

show(players_df[['MVP Rank', 'Player' ,'mvp_score', 'Age', 'Team', 'Pos', 'PTS', 'mvp_score', 'AST', 'TRB','BLK', 'STL','team_win_pct', '3P%_norm', '2P%_norm']].sort_values('MVP Rank')) # this shows the MVP data in a nice table
```

```{python}
#| layout: [[1,1,1,]]
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show code"
import plotly.express as px
#import seaborn as sns
fig = px.scatter(players_df, x="PTS", y="mvp_score", hover_name="Player", title="How does points per game relate to MVP score?", template="plotly_dark", width=500, height=400)

fig.show()

fig = px.scatter(players_df, x="AST", y="mvp_score", hover_name="Player", title="How does assists per game relate to MVP score?", template="plotly_dark", width=500, height=400)
fig.show()

fig = px.scatter(players_df, x="team_win_pct", y="mvp_score", hover_name="Player", title="How does the winning percentage relate to MVP score?", template="plotly_dark", width=500, height=400)
fig.show() 

fig = px.scatter(players_df, x="3P%_norm", y="mvp_score", hover_name="Player", title="How does ones' three-point efficiency relate to their MVP score?", template="plotly_dark", width=500, height=400)
fig.show()
```
